chunks: And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
He was asked about a man whom death approaches and he divorces his wife: is his divorce valid? He said: “Yes. If he dies, she inherits from him; and if she dies, he does not inherit from her.”

key_terms.فَيُطَلِّقُ: then he divorces; he issues a divorce
key_terms.لَمْ يَرِثْهَا: he does not inherit from her
key_terms.يَحْضُرُهُ الْمَوْتُ: death is approaching him; being in the illness or state near death

ai.seo_question: Is the divorce of a man on his deathbed valid, and do inheritance rules still apply?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the divorce of a man during the illness of death. The Imam عليه السلام affirms the validity of the divorce while also stating a specific inheritance consequence: if the husband dies, the divorced wife inherits from him, but if she dies, he does not inherit from her.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4882 - In a narration from Hammad through Al-Halabi, it is reported that Abu Abdullah (as) was asked about a man who was on his deathbed and divorced his wife. He was asked whether such a divorce was permissible.
Imam (as) replied: "Yes, it is permissible. If he dies, she will inherit from him, but if she dies, he will not inherit from her."
